uncited: *   **Input:** A pre-generated Sparse Voxel Octree (STree) representing the scene geometry; camera position and orientation; user interaction commands (Union/Subtraction via screen pick).
*   **Output:** A 64-bit framebuffer containing position and albedo for opaque voxels; a modified STree and voxel pool reflecting real-time changes.
**STree (Streaming Tree):** A two-level structure.
*   **High-level:** A 2D uniform grid of chunks.
*   **Low-level:** A sparse octree within each chunk.
Uses a distance-based error metric to determine which cells to stream.
Sets itself apart by using a simple scalar multiplier (`LOD_factor`) rather than complex geometric error metrics.
Choose when memory bandwidth is a bottleneck and scene scale is massive. [Link to [Streaming LOD](link)].
Uses a 64-bit visibility buffer to decouple geometry reconstruction from shading.
Sets itself apart by enabling efficient reconstruction of voxel cubes from point data.
Choose when rendering large numbers of small primitives efficiently. [Link to [Visibility Buffer Rendering](link)].
Supports Union and Subtraction via screen picking and re-voxelization.
Sets itself apart by allowing direct modification of the sparse voxel structure in real-time.
Choose when interactive editing of voxel scenes is required. [Link to [Real-Time Voxel Modification](link)].
*   **Time Complexity:** Streaming is logarithmic with respect to scene depth (octree traversal).
Voxelization is linear with respect to the number of voxels in a cell ($64^3$).
Rendering is linear with respect to the number of visible voxels.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of streamed cells.
Each cell consumes a page of 16,384 voxels in the Voxel Pool.
*   **Strengths:** Real-time rendering of large-scale scenes ($4^{12}$); efficient real-time modification (Union/Subtraction); linear storage allows efficient streaming.
*   **When to Use:** Large-scale urban or environmental visualization where real-time editing is needed.
*   **When Not to Use:** Scenes requiring transparency or complex lighting effects that require blending.
It builds on the concepts of Virtual Texture and Virtual Geometry, adapting them for voxel data.
